item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B implements the frozen contract directly and with minimal scope, while Candidate A changes the required API, bypasses Add, and introduces explicitly forbidden functionality and unrelated retry machinery.","reasons":["B adds the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption) (*File, error). A instead accepts ...UploadFileOption, creating a different public API.","B reuses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), producing the required replayable multipart body with the correct field and filename.","B routes Upload through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving existing option handling, request construction, decoding, and error semantics in one place. A duplicates Add's request and response logic inside Upload.","B validates empty filenames and nil content before encoding or sending a request, and its source-reader error test verifies propagation without a request being made. A does not visibly test source-reader failures despite the contract requiring itch coverage. It also creates new association options and arbitrary multipart fields, directly contradicting the instruction not to add association fields or change FilesOption behavior, while B leaves FilesOption unchanged."],"risks_a":["Its Upload signature violates the frozen public API contract by introducing UploadFileOption.","It does not route Upload through FilesService.Add and duplicates request/response behavior.","It adds association fields, WithFileFormValue, new option interfaces, and NewFileWithFields despite explicit scope prohibitions beyond what was requested and may alter body ownership semantics for existing callers."],"risks_b":["The retry test validates multipart contents only on the retried request rather than asserting both attempts carried identical complete bodies; the separate multipart test still covers encoding correctness.","No changelog or documentation update is included, though neither is required by the frozen contract."]}
